titre: Legally recognizing my child when we are not married
resume: Before or after the birth, free of charge at any town hall: recognition (reconnaissance) establishes the father's legal parentage. The two documents to bring and the effects on parental authority.
aQuoiCaSert: When the parents are not married, the father's legal parentage is not automatic: he must recognize the child. The mother has nothing to do if her name appears on the birth certificate. Recognition can be done before the birth (reconnaissance anticipée, prenatal recognition), when the birth is registered, or later. If done before the child's first birthday, it allows the father to exercise parental authority jointly with the mother.
quiEstConcerne: A mother who wishes to make a prenatal recognition (optional).
Female couples: a joint prenatal recognition is required (a separate procedure).
aSavoir: Recognition is free at any town hall (mairie), whatever the place of birth, your address or your nationality. It can also be done with a notary, for a fee (€75.46 excluding tax), if you want confidentiality.
Each parent can recognize the child without the other's agreement. No pregnancy certificate is required for a prenatal recognition. The document is drawn up immediately and you are given a copy.

Recognition after the birth: it is noted in the margin of the birth certificate and in the family record book (livret de famille), and the town hall informs the other parent by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt.
Recognition by both parents together: both must be present, each with proof of address in their own name.

A father who recognizes the child after their first birthday does not exercise parental authority. He can obtain it through a joint declaration with the mother (Cerfa n° 12785, in 3 copies, at the court registry (greffe) of the tribunal judiciaire or the tribunal de proximité where the child lives) or by applying to the family court judge (juge aux affaires familiales, JAF).

The parents marrying after the birth does not automatically give the father parental authority. Nor does the joint declaration change the child's surname: choosing the name requires a separate declaration.
If the child already has legal parentage established with another man, it must first be challenged in court.
